# fivenines_php_fpm_pools (Data Source)

The per-pool process state behind the instance's PHP-FPM view -- which pool ran out of workers, and when it last happened.

READ `max_children_reached_at`, NOT `max_children_reached`. The counter is CUMULATIVE since php-fpm started, so a non-zero value means "this has happened at some point", not "it is happening now", and it resets on a reload. `max_children_reached_at` is set only when the counter actually INCREASED between two agent ticks, which makes it the durable exhaustion signal; `children_exhausted` applies the product's 5-minute window to it.

Null gauges are "the agent did not report this field on the last tick", never zero: a pool with a null `active_processes` is unknown, not idle.

This collector is config-driven with no version floor, so `collector.supported` here means "the agent has not said it cannot" -- an agent predating the collector answers `true` with an empty list. Check `collector.last_reported_at` and the agent version before concluding the instance runs none.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_php_fpm_pools" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
}

# Read max_children_reached_at, not max_children_reached: the counter is
# cumulative since php-fpm started and resets on a reload, so a non-zero value
# means "at some point", not "right now".
output "pools_that_ran_out_of_workers" {
  value = [
    for p in data.fivenines_php_fpm_pools.all.php_fpm_pools :
    p.name if p.max_children_reached_at != null
  ]
}

# children_exhausted applies the product's own 5-minute window to that stamp.
output "pools_exhausted_now" {
  value = [
    for p in data.fivenines_php_fpm_pools.all.php_fpm_pools :
    p.saturation_detail if p.children_exhausted
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the pool name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over the collector's 10-minute sync window. `false` returns only rows the agent refreshed inside it -- the set you may read as CURRENT state; `true` returns the rest. The two values partition the collection (a row that never synced counts as stale). Omit for both.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `php_fpm_pools` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--php_fpm_pools))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--php_fpm_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `php_fpm_pools`

Read-Only:

- `accepted_connections` (Number) Cumulative, same caveat as above.
- `active_processes` (Number) Workers currently serving a request.
- `children_exhausted` (Boolean) max_children_reached_at falls inside the product's 5-minute window. This is the "pool exhausted right now" reading.
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `idle_processes` (Number) Workers idle right now. **Null means not reported, not 0.**
- `last_synced_at` (String) When the agent last refreshed this row.
- `listen_queue` (Number) Requests waiting to be accepted right now.
- `max_children_reached` (Number) CUMULATIVE count of times the process manager hit its child ceiling since php-fpm started. Resets on a reload. A non-zero value does NOT mean the pool is exhausted now.
- `max_children_reached_at` (String) THE durable exhaustion signal: set only when max_children_reached actually INCREASED between two agent ticks. Null means it has never happened while we were watching.
- `max_listen_queue` (Number) High-water mark since php-fpm started.
- `name` (String) The pool name, as configured in the pool's own php-fpm config.
- `process_manager` (String) The pool's process manager mode (`static`, `dynamic`, `ondemand`). Null when not reported.
- `queue_saturated` (Boolean) A request was sitting in the listen queue on the last tick.
- `saturated` (Boolean) Either saturation signal, at the product's default thresholds.
- `saturation_detail` (String) Which signal(s) fired, e.g. "listen queue at 12, hit max_children", or "healthy".
- `slow_requests` (Number) Cumulative, same caveat as above.
- `stale` (Boolean) True when the agent stopped refreshing this row (outside the 10-minute sync window, or never synced). These tables are only updated while an agent keeps reporting, so a problem row on a dead agent reads as a problem forever -- check this before acting on the state above.
- `total_processes` (Number) Workers alive right now. **Null means not reported, not 0.**
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
